title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
core_method: method
datasets: Low-rank weight decomposition W+BA with r<<min(d
baselines: k); merge into original weights for zero inference overhead
key_evidence: Accuracy/BLEU/GPU memory
limitations: Yes (HuggingFace PEFT)
relevance_to_project: Matches/exceeds full fine-tuning across RoBERTa/DeBERTa/GPT-2/GPT-3
column20: Rank selection heuristic; NLP-originated may not be optimal for vision
column21: Cornerstone PEFT method; r=8-16 fits 16GB VRAM

title: CoOp/CoCoOp: Learning to Prompt for Vision-Language Models
research_problem: Replace hand-crafted CLIP prompts with learnable continuous vectors
core_method: Learnable context vectors (CoOp static; CoCoOp instance-conditional via meta-network)
key_evidence: 16-shot CoOp 63.33% vs CLIP zero-shot 56.77%; CoCoOp Harmonic mean 75.83%
limitations: CoOp overfits to base classes; CoCoOp inference 160ms/image vs 6ms
relevance_to_project: Standard CLIP PEFT starting point

title: VPT: Visual Prompt Tuning
research_problem: First systematic prompt tuning for pure vision encoders
core_method: Learnable prompt tokens in ViT input space; VPT-Shallow (first layer) and VPT-Deep (every layer)
key_evidence: Outperforms full fine-tuning in 20/24 tasks; especially strong in low-data regimes
limitations: Requires tuning prompt count per task; prompts add inference cost
relevance_to_project: Core baseline for pure vision PEFT

title: SSF: Scaling & Shifting Your Features
research_problem: Can only 0.3M params surpass full fine-tuning?
core_method: Learnable scale+shift per operation (MSA/MLP/LayerNorm); re-parameterization for zero inference overhead
limitations: Linear-only may be insufficient for large domain gaps
relevance_to_project: Best for extreme budget: 0.3M params + zero inference overhead

title: AdaptFormer: Adapting Vision Transformers
research_problem: Replace frozen ViT MLP with learnable adapter for video
core_method: Parallel AdaptMLP (down-proj→ReLU→up-proj+residual) with <2% extra params
key_evidence: +10% SSv2; +19% HMDB51 vs full FT with 1.5% extra params
limitations: Adapters add inference latency (unlike LoRA/SSF)
relevance_to_project: Important adapter baseline for video

title: Tip-Adapter: Training-Free Adaptation of CLIP
research_problem: Can CLIP adapt without any SGD?
core_method: Key-value cache from few-shot features; cosine similarity retrieval blended with CLIP zero-shot prediction
key_evidence: Comparable to CoOp/CLIP-Adapter without SGD; Tip-Adapter-F SOTA with ~10x fewer epochs
limitations: Cache grows with few-shot samples; retrieval adds test latency
relevance_to_project: Training-free baseline for budget-aware scenarios

title: MaPLe: Multi-modal Prompt Learning
research_problem: First coupled vision-language prompt learning
core_method: Vision-language prompt coupling function; deep prompting in both branches
code_available: SOTA multi-modal prompting for understanding trade-offs

title: KgCoOp: Knowledge-Guided Context Optimization
research_problem: Prevent catastrophic forgetting of CLIP knowledge in prompt tuning
core_method: Euclidean distance regularization between learned and hand-crafted prompt embeddings
key_evidence: Harmonic mean 77.0; New accuracy 73.6 (best); training speed=CoOp (6ms/img)
limitations: Regularization strength lambda is dataset-dependent
relevance_to_project: Simple effective regularization principle; transferable design philosophy

title: PromptSRC: Self-Regulating Prompts
research_problem: Can we achieve SOTA prompt tuning with only 46K params?
core_method: Mutual agreement maximization+Gaussian prompt aggregation+textual diversity
key_evidence: Harmonic mean 79.97% (+1.42% MaPLe); only 46K params
limitations: Three regularization components add implementation complexity
relevance_to_project: Best prompt learning for parameter efficiency; 46K params ideal for 16GB

title: PLOT: Prompt Learning with Optimal Transport
research_problem: Learn multiple diverse prompts aligned with local image regions
core_method: Optimal transport (Sinkhorn) for multi-prompt-vision alignment
key_evidence: Significantly outperforms CoOp; fine-grained matching avoids single-prompt convergence
limitations: 4 prompts/class increase params; Sinkhorn entropy needs tuning
relevance_to_project: Multi-prompt diversity mechanism; OT framework theoretically elegant

title: Convpass: Convolutional Bypasses for ViT Adapters
research_problem: NLP-ported PEFT lack visual inductive bias; can conv fix this?
core_method: Convolutional bottleneck blocks in parallel with frozen transformer blocks; 2D spatial structure restoration
key_evidence: VTAB-1K 76.6% (vs LoRA 74.5%/full FT 68.9%); 0.33M params
limitations: Conv design tailored to ViT; not directly applicable to other architectures
relevance_to_project: KEY INSIGHT: vision-tailored PEFT outperforms NLP-ported PEFT on vision

title: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
research_problem: Can decomposing weights into magnitude+direction improve LoRA?
core_method: W = m*(V/||V||) + BA; magnitude learned independently; direction low-rank updated
key_evidence: Consistently outperforms LoRA on vision-language tasks; no inference overhead
limitations: Slightly more complex; magnitude learning adds d params
relevance_to_project: Potential upgrade over standard LoRA; extra capacity may help very low-shot

title: Lessons from a Unifying Study of PEFT in Visual Recognition
research_problem: How different are PEFT methods really when properly tuned?
core_method: Hyperparameter-tuned comparison of VPT/Adapter/LoRA/BitFit/SSF on VTAB-1K
metrics: Top-1 accuracy; robustness to distribution shift
key_evidence: (1) ALL methods similar when tuned; (2) complementary errors enable ensembles; (3) PEFT preserves robustness better than full FT
limitations: VTAB-1K only; HP tuning itself expensive
relevance_to_project: THE key motivation: method selection matters less than auto HP tuning→ supports project thesis

title: Fine-tuning LLMs with Limited Data: Survey and Guide
research_problem: Best practices for fine-tuning under limited data and GPU budget?
core_method: Survey codifying: QLoRA as default; moderate LoRA rank (16-32); top-2 layer freezing; data quality>quantity
key_evidence: QLoRA on quantized larger model > full FT on smaller model; random search reduces HP time 30%; 100K tokens continued pre-training effective
limitations: NLP-focused; vision PEFT not extensively covered
relevance_to_project: Directly applicable guidelines: QLoRA+rank 16-32=16GB GPU optimal

title: CLIP-Adapter: Better Vision-Language Models with Feature Adapters
research_problem: Can simple feature adapters improve CLIP few-shot?
core_method: Bottleneck adapter on CLIP visual/visual+textual features
key_evidence: Competitive or better than CoOp with simpler design; no prompt engineering needed
limitations: Adapter adds inference cost (unlike prompt methods)
relevance_to_project: Simple adapter baseline; SJTU+CUHK=Chinese-relevant

title: Hyperband
research_problem: Accelerate random search via adaptive resource allocation+early stopping
core_method: Successive halving in multiple brackets; poor configs pruned aggressively
key_evidence: >10x speedup vs BO; near-optimal theoretical guarantees
limitations: Requires max/min resource+reduction factor; random sampling (no model)
relevance_to_project: Foundational multi-fidelity HPO; resource allocation directly applicable

title: BOHB: Robust and Efficient HPO at Scale
research_problem: Combine Hyperband's speed with BO's sample efficiency
core_method: Hyperband bracket scheduling+TPE (KDE-based l(x)/g(x)) with random fraction
key_evidence: 10-100x faster to lowest test error; ResNet-20: 2.78±0.09%
limitations: Surrogate bias from low-fidelity signals; sensitivity to eta
relevance_to_project: Most practical multi-fidelity BO for single GPU budget constraints

title: DEHB: Evolutionary Hyperband
research_problem: BOHB's TPE has O(n^3) overhead; can evolution be cheaper?
core_method: Differential Evolution replaces TPE; Hyperband successive halving; constant overhead
key_evidence: Up to 1000x faster than RS; up to 32x faster than BOHB; strong on high-dim discrete
limitations: DE mutation requires continuous conversion; sub-population complexity
relevance_to_project: Well-suited for NAS+high-dim HPO under budget constraints

title: HEBO: Pushing Limits of Sample-Efficient HPO
research_problem: Are GP's homoscedasticity+stationarity assumptions violated in real HPO?
core_method: Non-linear input/output warping+multi-objective acquisition ensemble (Pareto front)
key_evidence: Significantly outperforms existing optimizers across 108 tasks; heteroscedasticity is pervasive
limitations: GP surrogates still O(n^3); warping adds hyper-hyperparams
relevance_to_project: Explains why naive GP-BO fails: noise varies dramatically across HP regions in fine-tuning

title: SMAC3: Versatile Bayesian Optimization
research_problem: Robust BO framework for mixed/categorical/conditional search spaces
core_method: Random Forest surrogates (C++ backend)+aggressive racing (intensification)+multiple facades
key_evidence: Powers SOTA AutoML systems; RF handles mixed spaces naturally; racing=built-in early stopping
limitations: RF less sample-efficient than GP for low-dim continuous; sequential by design
relevance_to_project: Most practical BO for heterogeneous search spaces in budget-constrained AutoML

title: LC-PFN: Efficient Bayesian Learning Curve Extrapolation
research_problem: Can LCE achieve Bayesian inference in single forward pass?
core_method: Transformer pre-trained on 10M synthetic right-censored curves; single forward pass=posterior predictive
key_evidence: ~10,000x faster than MCMC; predictive early stop=2-6x speedup on 45/53 datasets
limitations: PFN trained on synthetic only; sensitive to real noise
relevance_to_project: Near-zero-cost early stopping — core component for budget-aware agent

title: FT-PFN/iFBO: In-Context Freeze-Thaw BO
research_problem: Can freeze-thaw BO avoid online surrogate retraining?
core_method: FT-PFN surrogate+MFPI-random acquisition; single forward pass at inference
key_evidence: 10-100x faster predictions; new SOTA on 3 suites; synthetic-trained PFN generalizes to real curves
limitations: Requires PFN pre-training; MFPI-random is myopic
relevance_to_project: State of the art in cost-sensitive HPO — optimal resource allocation

title: DyHPO: Supervising the Multi-Fidelity Race
research_problem: Can dynamic allocation policy replace fixed Hyperband schedules?
core_method: Deep kernel GP surrogate embeds learning curve dynamics; multi-budget acquisition; dynamic racing
key_evidence: Significant superiority over SOTA on 50 datasets; adapts to problem characteristics
limitations: Deep kernel GP adds training overhead; requires careful HP tuning
relevance_to_project: Dynamic racing directly relevant — adaptive resource allocation for limited GPU hours

title: FanG-HPO: Fair and Green HPO
research_problem: Optimize accuracy+fairness+energy simultaneously in HPO?
core_method: Multi-objective BO+dataset subsets as cheap information sources
key_evidence: Explicit accuracy-fairness-energy trade-off; cheap proxy evaluations reduce total energy
limitations: Focus on fairness; subsetting may not work for already-small data
relevance_to_project: Multi-information-source concept directly applicable — cheap data subset evaluations

title: Strategies of AutoML for Green AI
research_problem: Can HPO be made significantly greener without accuracy loss?
core_method: Energy efficiency metrics for HPO algorithms; compares BOHB/HyperBand/PBT/ASHA under energy-aware metrics
key_evidence: 28.7% CO2 reduction with only 0.51% accuracy decrease; ASHA+PBT more energy-efficient than BOHB
limitations: Single study; energy depends on hardware+grid mix
relevance_to_project: Quantifies energy-performance trade-off — key evidence for budget-aware design

title: XAutoLM: Efficient Fine-Tuning via Meta-Learning and AutoML
research_problem: Joint model selection+HPO for LM fine-tuning under compute constraints?
core_method: Task-level+system-level meta-features from past experiments; experience-aware prior biases sampling; supports LoRA
key_evidence: 4.5x mean evaluation time reduction; 7x search error ratio reduction; 5/6 tasks > zero-shot
limitations: Single-domain (NLP); requires experience database
relevance_to_project: MOST DIRECTLY RELEVANT: meta-learning accelerates AutoML but NLP-only (vision gap=our contribution)

title: DHA: End-to-End Joint Optimization of DA+HPO+Architecture
research_problem: Can DA policy+HP+architecture be jointly optimized without retraining?
core_method: Differentiable NAS in compressed feature space; DA+HPO as dynamic schedulers; ready-to-use model
key_evidence: First joint end-to-end optimization of all three components; no retraining needed
limitations: Differentiable only; limited to continuous HPs; CV only
relevance_to_project: Joint optimization principle critical for budget-aware AutoML

title: GPBT: Generalized Population-Based Training
research_problem: Can learned perturbation improve PBT over random perturbation?
core_method: Pairwise Learning: pseudo-gradients from paired agent performance guide underperformers
key_evidence: 24-32% improvement over standard PBT; more robust to perturbation intervals
limitations: RL-only; requires parallel population
relevance_to_project: PBT/GPBT as alternative to sequential BO; viable if running concurrent trials on 16GB

title: FedPop: Federated Population-based Hyperparameter Tuning
research_problem: Joint optimization of client+server HPs in federated learning?
core_method: Online tuning-while-training population-based evolutionary framework
key_evidence: First to jointly optimize client+server HPs in FL; validated on full ImageNet-1K
limitations: FL-specific; distributed infrastructure needed
relevance_to_project: Demonstrates population-based HPO viable for complex settings

title: HPOBench: Reproducible Multi-Fidelity HPO Benchmarks
research_problem: HPO lacks standardized reproducible benchmarks
core_method: 100+ multi-fidelity problems across 12 families; Singularity containers for reproducibility
key_evidence: Container-based reproducibility; multi-fidelity methods provide substantial early speedups
limitations: Singularity requires Linux; raw benchmarks still expensive to run
relevance_to_project: Standardized way to benchmark budget-aware HPO methods

title: YAHPO Gym: Multi-Objective Multi-Fidelity HPO Benchmark
research_problem: Tabular benchmarks can mislead; can surrogate benchmarks be better?
core_method: 14 scenarios 700+ problems; ONNX-compressed ResNet surrogates; 10-100ms per eval
key_evidence: Faster and more faithful than tabular benchmarks; Spearman's rho typically >0.7
limitations: Surrogates are approximations; may miss discontinuities
relevance_to_project: Enables cheap statistically rigorous comparison of budget-aware HPO without GPU clusters

title: FlexHB: More Efficient and Flexible HPO Framework
research_problem: Fixed Hyperband brackets ignore problem-specific optimal schedules
core_method: Fine-grained fidelity+FlexBand (adaptive SH bracket allocation with global ranking)
key_evidence: 6.9x vs MFES-HB; 11.1x vs BOHB; 4.9-16x vs Hyperband
limitations: Preprint only; adaptive allocation adds complexity
relevance_to_project: Directly addresses fixed-bracket limitation for budget-aware fine-tuning

title: Low-Budget Optimization Comparison
research_problem: Is BO always best under low evaluation budgets?
core_method: Comprehensive comparison of BO-based vs classical DFO vs evolutionary methods
key_evidence: BO best at limited budgets; outperformed by CMA-ES/DE as budget increases; BO efficiency decreases with dimension
limitations: BBOB focuses on synthetic functions; not standard ML HPO
relevance_to_project: Direct answer: BO is right for 10-50 trials; classical methods catch up with more

title: The AI Scientist v1
research_problem: Can LLM autonomously conduct full scientific research cycle?
core_method: LLM pipeline: idea gen→code→experiment→LaTeX paper→automated peer review
key_evidence: Produces 10 papers; some reach 'Weak Accept'; per-paper ~$15
limitations: 42% experiment failure rate; 57% manuscripts with hallucinations; automated reviewer rejects 9/10 human papers
relevance_to_project: Foundational end-to-end system; understanding failure modes is key

title: The AI Scientist v2
research_problem: Can autonomous agent explore without human templates using principled search?
core_method: Progressive best-first tree search; removes human templates; VLM figure quality feedback; multi-LLM
key_evidence: First AI-generated paper accepted at ICLR workshop; exceeds average human acceptance threshold
limitations: Lower success rate than v1 (broader search space); cost scales with tree width
relevance_to_project: Tree search improves autonomous discovery over linear pipelines

title: PaperQA2
research_problem: Can LLM agents surpass humans at literature search/summarization/contradiction detection?
core_method: RAG agent: Paper Search→Gather Evidence→Generate Answer→Citation Traversal
key_evidence: Superhuman on all 3 literature tasks; WikiCrow > human Wikipedia articles
limitations: Limited to literature tasks; $1-3/query
relevance_to_project: Gold standard for literature review agents

title: ChemCrow: Augmenting LLMs with Chemistry Tools
research_problem: Can augmenting LLMs with expert chemistry tools bridge the reasoning gap?
core_method: GPT-4+18 expert-designed chemistry tools (SMILES/Reaction prediction/Safety/IUPAC) using ReAct
datasets: 14 chemical use cases; real-world synthesis of DEET+organocatalysts
key_evidence: Expert chemists preferred ChemCrow over GPT-4 alone on complex tasks
limitations: GPT-4 alone better on simple tasks; evaluator LLM cannot replace expert assessment
relevance_to_project: Classic tool-augmented LLM for science; value from tools not LLM

title: Coscientist: Autonomous Chemical Research with LLMs
research_problem: Can single LLM autonomously plan+execute multi-step chemical experiments?
core_method: GPT-4: Planning+Web Search+Hardware Documentation+Data Analysis+Code Execution modules
key_evidence: Successfully planned 7 molecule syntheses; Nobel Prize-winning reactions in <4 minutes
limitations: Safety concerns require human-in-the-loop; limited to established reactions
relevance_to_project: Seminal LLM-controlled physical experimentation demonstration

title: SciAgents: Multi-Agent Intelligent Graph Reasoning
research_problem: Can ensemble of specialized LLM agents generate cross-disciplinary hypotheses?
core_method: Multi-agent (Ontologist/Scientist1/Scientist2/Critic/Planner) over knowledge graph; GPT-4 via ICL
code_available: Semantic Scholar novelty check/human expert assessment
key_evidence: Yes (github.com/lamm-mit/SciAgentsDiscovery)
limitations: Novel silk+dandelion pigment hypotheses; discovered unconsidered interdisciplinary relationships
relevance_to_project: Domain-specific; static knowledge graph; hypotheses not experimentally validated
column20: Best multi-agent hypothesis generation with structured knowledge

title: Data Interpreter: LLM Agent for Data Science
research_problem: Standard LLM agents struggle with data science: real-time adjustments+dependencies
core_method: Dynamic planning with hierarchical graphs+dynamic tool integration+logical inconsistency detection
key_evidence: ML tasks 0.86→0.95; MATH +26%; open-ended +112%; DABench +25%
limitations: Relies on GPT-4 level models; hierarchical planning brittle with unexpected data
relevance_to_project: Structured planning+error detection value proposition

title: AIDE: AI-Driven Exploration in the Space of Code
research_problem: Can ML engineering be framed as code optimization via tree search?
core_method: Solution Space Tree Search: nodes=Python scripts; ops=draft/debug/improve; search policy selects
key_evidence: 4x medals vs best linear agent; 92.4% valid submission vs 63.6% OpenHands; MLE-bench dominant scaffold
limitations: Hard-coded search policy; struggles with large codebases; greedy local optima
relevance_to_project: Dominant MLE-bench agent scaffold; hard-coded search>learned=value from orchestration

title: MLAgentBench: Evaluating Language Agents on ML Experimentation
research_problem: How to systematically benchmark LLM agents on open-ended ML experimentation?
core_method: 15-task suite (CIFAR-10 to BabyLM); ReAct framework; competence+reasoning+efficiency evaluation
key_evidence: Claude v3 Opus 37.5% avg; ~90% CIFAR-10; ~10% recent Kaggle; 0% newest research
limitations: Limited to 15 tasks; performance dependent on task recency
relevance_to_project: Foundational ML agent benchmark; ReAct evaluation paradigm

title: MLE-bench: Evaluating ML Agents on ML Engineering
research_problem: Can AI agents perform as ML engineers on real-world competitions?
core_method: 75 Kaggle competitions (tabular/image/NLP/multimodal); 3 difficulty levels; anti-cheating
key_evidence: o1-preview+AIDE: 16.9% medal (pass@1)/34.1% (8 attempts); AIDE 4:1 medals vs OpenHands
limitations: Kaggle data contamination risk; anti-cheating not foolproof
relevance_to_project: De facto ML engineering agent benchmark; used by OpenAI Preparedness Framework

title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
research_problem: Can AI agents replicate SOTA ML papers from scratch?
core_method: 20 ICML 2024 Spotlight/Oral papers; 8316 gradable rubric tasks; LLM judge (F1=0.83)
key_evidence: Best agent (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) 21.0% vs human PhD 41.4%; o1 plateaued after 1h
limitations: Only 20 ICML papers; rubric creation requires author time; grading ~$66/paper MOST RIGOROUS test of autonomous AI research capability

title: MLR-Bench: Evaluating Agents on Open-Ended ML Research
research_problem: How to evaluate end-to-end ML research including idea→experiment→paper?
core_method: 201 workshop tasks; MLR-Judge (LLM reviewer with expert-validated rubrics); MLR-Agent scaffold
key_evidence: **~80% agent-produced experimental results are fabricated or invalid** — LLMs write coherent papers but fail at valid experimentation
limitations: Workshop scope; LLM judge limitations
relevance_to_project: Most direct evidence of fabricated results problem; critical for understanding failure rates

title: CORE-Bench: Computational Reproducibility Agent Benchmark
research_problem: Can AI agents verify computational reproducibility of published research?
core_method: 270 tasks from 90 papers across CS/social science/medicine; 3 difficulty levels; isolated VM
key_evidence: Best agent: 58-60% easy; 19-21% hardest; v1.1 near-ceiling saturation with GPT-5.4+Codex CLI
limitations: Only 3 disciplines; rapid saturation (v1.1)
relevance_to_project: If agents can't reproduce published work they can't do novel work

title: ScienceAgentBench: Toward Rigorous Assessment for Scientific Discovery
research_problem: Rigorous assessment of LLM agents on individual data-driven scientific tasks
core_method: 102 tasks from 44 peer-reviewed publications; 4 disciplines; validated by 9 SMEs
key_evidence: Best agent 32.4% independent/34.3% with expert knowledge; o1-preview 42.2% at >10x cost
limitations: 4 disciplines only; tasks are individual steps not full pipelines
relevance_to_project: Even individual scientific coding tasks remain challenging

title: LMR-BENCH: Reproducing Language Modeling Research
research_problem: Can agents reproduce code from NLP papers requiring abstract concept synthesis?
core_method: 28 code reproduction tasks from 23 NLP papers; 9 categories; unit test+LLM evaluation
key_evidence: Even most advanced models exhibit persistent limitations in scientific reasoning and code synthesis from NLP papers
limitations: 28 tasks only; NLP-specific; no published quantitative failure rates
relevance_to_project: Focused test of code reproduction from papers — fundamental capability

title: PiML: Automated ML Workflow Optimization using LLM Agents
research_problem: Can iterative agentic reasoning surpass AIDE for end-to-end ML workflows?
core_method: Multi-agent: iterative Thought-Action-Observation+Debug Chain+adaptive memory; o3-mini
key_evidence: 41.0% Above Median vs 30.8%; 29.5% Medal vs 23.1%; 44.7% Percentile vs 38.8%
limitations: Single model tested (o3-mini); adaptive memory may lose context in long runs
relevance_to_project: Systematic debugging+adaptive memory > tree-search-only (AIDE)

title: ML-Master: Integration of Exploration and Reasoning
research_problem: Can balanced exploration-reasoning surpass MLE-bench leaders?
core_method: MCTS-inspired tree search+steerable reasoning with adaptive memory; DeepSeek-R1 backbone
key_evidence: Medal 29.3% (12h)/56.44% (ML-Master 2.0/24h); 93.3% valid submission; 44.9% above median
limitations: Still far from human expert on hard tasks
relevance_to_project: SOTA MLE-bench; value of integrating MCTS exploration with reasoning

title: Independent Evaluation of Sakana's AI Scientist
research_problem: Are AI Scientist's bold claims of autonomous discovery supported?
core_method: Installed+running AI Scientist v1 on 2 computers; MovieLens-100k; systematic output analysis
baselines: AI Scientist's own claims; human researcher baseline
key_evidence: 42% experiment failure; 57% hallucinated manuscripts; 100% novelty misclassification; +8% chars/iteration code modification
limitations: Single dataset; single template; GPT-4o only; v1 only
relevance_to_project: MOST SOBERING data on actual failure rates; essential before making any autonomous agent claims

title: Deep Learning for Digitisation of Complex Documents and Engineering Diagrams
research_problem: Comprehensive critical survey of DL for engineering drawing processing
core_method: Systematically reviews CNN/Transformer/hybrid methods for P&ID/floor plans/construction
key_evidence: DL adoption significantly increasing since 2018; key challenge: lack of public datasets
limitations: Lacks VLM coverage (too early)
relevance_to_project: Foundational orientation: data scarcity+annotation difficulty=genuine research barriers

title: P&ID Digitization with Transformers + PID2Graph Dataset
research_problem: End-to-end graph extraction from P&IDs
core_method: Relationformer (DETR variant): simultaneous object+relationship detection; first public P&ID graph dataset
key_evidence: +25% edge detection over modular baselines on real data
limitations: Single industrial domain (Oil & Gas); no semantic validation
relevance_to_project: Strongest baseline for image-to-structured-graph recovery

title: Fine-Tuning VLM for Automated GD&T Extraction
research_problem: Can small fine-tuned VLM beat large zero-shot VLM on GD&T?
core_method: Fine-tuned Florence-2 (0.23B) vs zero-shot GPT-4o/Claude-3.5-Sonnet
key_evidence: +29.95% precision; +37.75% recall; +52.4% F1; -43.15% hallucination
limitations: Small dataset (400); single GD&T task; generalization untested
relevance_to_project: Small fine-tuned VLMs > large zero-shot on specialized engineering tasks; directly supports auto-fine-tuning validation

title: FlowLearn: Evaluating LVLMs on Flowchart Understanding
research_problem: Standardized LVLM flowchart understanding benchmark
core_method: 3858 scientific+10000 simulated (Mermaid.js) flowcharts; 5 task types
metrics: Accuracy per task/F1 Mermaid code gen
key_evidence: GPT-4V 58% node counting; Claude Opus 83% OCR; **all models <50% F1 link-level Mermaid**
limitations: Simulated flowcharts may be simpler than real engineering diagrams
relevance_to_project: Demonstrates even SOTA LVLMs fail at compositional structural reasoning

title: TextFlow: Intermediate Text Representation for Flowchart QA
research_problem: End-to-end VLMs lack controllability/explainability for flowchart QA
core_method: Vision Textualizer (flowchart→Graphviz/Mermaid/PlantUML)+Textual Reasoner (LLM)
key_evidence: SOTA on both benchmarks with improved robustness and explainability
limitations: Vision Textualizer can propagate errors; text format choice affects downstream
relevance_to_project: Decouple vision from reasoning: highly relevant for auto-fine-tuning pipeline design

title: GraphDecoder: Recovering Network Graphs from Visualization Images
research_problem: Recover diverse network graphs (mind maps/flowcharts/E-R) from raster images
core_method: Attention-enhanced U-Net semantic segmentation+custom graph extraction loss
key_evidence: Effective recovery of diverse graph types; interactive redesign interface
limitations: U-Net architecture (pre-VLM era); limited to known visual styles
relevance_to_project: Establishes image-to-graph recovery problem formally

title: DesignQA: Multimodal Benchmark for Engineering Documentation Understanding
research_problem: Can MLLMs reason about engineering requirements from text+CAD+drawings?
core_method: 3 task categories: Rule Comprehension/Compliance/Extraction; Formula SAE documents+CAD
key_evidence: MLLMs struggle with rule retrieval+technical component recognition+drawing analysis
limitations: Single domain (Formula SAE); limited model set
relevance_to_project: Directly tests Cluster D core hypothesis: can VLMs reason about engineering diagrams in context?

title: Draw with Thought: Unleashing Multimodal Reasoning for Scientific Diagrams
research_problem: Recover editable structured representations from raster scientific diagrams
core_method: CoT coarse-to-fine planning+structure-aware code generation+Draw.io Verifier refinement
key_evidence: 10-20% higher semantic alignment; 89% XML validity; human eval 7.3/10 similarity
limitations: Scientific conference diagrams (not industrial); training-free relies on MLLM
relevance_to_project: IMAGE-TO-STRUCTURED-GRAPH best method; mxGraph XML format+CLIP-score evaluation protocol directly adoptable

title: CAD2Program: From 2D CAD Drawings to 3D Parametric Models
research_problem: Reconstruct 3D parametric models from 2D CAD raster drawings
core_method: InternVL (Mini-InternVL 2B): ViT encodes raster→auto-regressive text shape programs (Python)
metrics: Model retrieval accuracy/3D reconstruction F1/parameter accuracy
key_evidence: 93.8% retrieval; 82.76% F1; 97.21% param accuracy; annotations +20% F1
limitations: Single domain (cabinets); text-based output constrains to predefined primitives
relevance_to_project: VLM-based diagram-to-structured-output pipeline; annotations are critical context

title: SysTemp: Multi-Agent System for Template-Based SysML v2 Generation
research_problem: LLMs fail at syntactically correct SysML v2 due to scarce training data
core_method: 4-agent system: SpecificationGenerator→TemplateGenerator (Jinja2)→Writer→Parser (ANTLR feedback)
datasets: Custom NL SysML v2 scenarios (5 reported)
key_evidence: 80% syntax correctness with skeleton vs 20% without; ≤3 refinement iterations
limitations: Small test set (5 scenarios); semantic correctness not evaluated; template constrains expressiveness
relevance_to_project: Establishes LLM+parser feedback loop for SysML v2

title: Agent-Based Approach for Valid SysMLv2 Model Generation
research_problem: Industrial-grade SysML v2 generation with 100% syntactic validity
core_method: LLM+RAG (curated SysML v2 examples)+ANTLR validation engine+diagnostic self-correction
key_evidence: **100% syntactic validity across 20 prompts**; outperforms LLM-only in ALL metrics
limitations: No semantic correctness evaluation; RAG dependency on curated examples
relevance_to_project: RAG+ANTLR+self-correcting loop=blueprint for SysML validation component

title: VQA for SysML Block Definition Diagrams
research_problem: Can MLLMs understand SysML v1 BDDs at Bloom's lower cognitive levels?
core_method: VQA tasks on SysML v1 BDDs at Bloom's Remember and Understand levels
metrics: Accuracy at Remember and Understand levels
key_evidence: MLLMs show basic BDD comprehension but limitations at higher-order reasoning
limitations: Limited to BDDs; lower Bloom's levels only; defense data may not be public
relevance_to_project: Pioneering VLM-SysML intersection; low baseline shows how poorly VLMs understand SysML

title: CircuitSense: Hierarchical Circuit Benchmark Exposing Perception-Reasoning Gap
research_problem: MLLMs perceive circuits but can they derive equations and do engineering reasoning?
core_method: 8006+ problems; 6 hierarchy levels (resistor→system block); 3 tasks: Perception/Analysis/Design
key_evidence: **Closed-source MLLMs: >85% perception but <19% symbolic derivation and analytical reasoning**
limitations: Synthetic circuits may miss real complexity; electrical domain only
relevance_to_project: Quantifies perception-reasoning gap—Cluster D's structured-graph recovery must close this

title: Beyond Pixels: Vector-to-Graph Framework for Reliable Schematic Auditing
research_problem: MLLMs suffer structural blindness on engineering schematics due to pixel-driven processing
core_method: V2G pipeline: CAD primitives→property graph (ezdxf)+GSP Verifier (Laplacian eigenvalues)
datasets: ~900 power utility engineering schematics; 3 compliance categories
key_evidence: Overall 12%→47% (MLLM→MLLM+V2G); connection labeling 6%→67% (+61%); ALL 6 MLLMs benefited
limitations: Requires vector CAD input; single utility domain; GSP is deterministic/rule-based
relevance_to_project: DIRECTLY validates Cluster D hypothesis: pixel-based VLM is fundamentally unreliable without graph structure

title: MBSE-Graph-RAG for Engineering Document Querying
research_problem: Can LLM+KG democratize MBSE tool access?
core_method: Knowledge graphs from unstructured engineering docs aligned with SysML standards; NL→graph query
key_evidence: Framework for bridging generative AI with MBSE data consolidation
limitations: Conceptual only; no quantitative benchmarks
relevance_to_project: Establishes RAG+KG paradigm for SysML/MBSE

title: AGREE-Dog Copilot: Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Enhanced MBSE
research_problem: Can LLM copilot automate formal verification counterexample repair for MBSE?
core_method: LLMs (GPT-4o/O3/GPT-4.1)+AGREE model checker; 16 automated DevOps steps; novel context selection
metrics: Repair rate/accuracy after N iterations/latency/human input
key_evidence: 84.6% 1-iteration; ~92% after 2; **100% within 3**; human <0.1% tokens; weeks→minutes
limitations: AADL-specific (not SysML directly); requires formal AGREE contracts
relevance_to_project: Demonstrates neuro-symbolic verification; 3-iteration convergence=north-star target

title: A Survey on Stability of Learning with Limited Labelled Data
research_problem: How does uncontrolled randomness affect FSL/meta-learning/PEFT stability?
core_method: Systematic analysis of 415 papers categorizing randomness effects on stability
key_evidence: Performance deviations up to 90% between min and max; seed changes can invert model rankings
limitations: Focused on categorization not solutions
relevance_to_project: Foundational for PEFT benchmark design: variance analysis is non-optional

title: PEFT-Bench: A Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Methods Benchmark
research_problem: First holistic end-to-end PEFT benchmark for autoregressive LLMs
core_method: 7 PEFT methods (LoRA/IA3/Prompt/P-Tuning/Prefix/LNTuning) on 27 NLP datasets; PEFT Soft Cost Penalties metric
key_evidence: LoRA best overall accuracy; LNTuning best PSCP; IA3 most stable
limitations: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct only; NO vision; NO cross-seed variance
relevance_to_project: First unified PEFT benchmark but doesn't cover vision or variance analysis (our gap)

title: Evaluating the Evaluators: Are Validation Methods for FSL Fit for Purpose?
research_problem: How accurately do different performance estimators work in FSL?
core_method: Systematic investigation of task-level validation accuracy for FSL; 5-fold CV/LOO-CV/bootstrapping
key_evidence: >50% chance validation accuracy wrong by >10 absolute points; best estimator MAE 9.5-12.7%; max Spearman 0.36
limitations: Limited to FSL tasks tested
relevance_to_project: Quantifies FSL evaluation unreliability: any PEFT benchmark must address this

title: Lessons from a Unifying Study of PEFT in Visual Recognition (diagnostic aspect)
research_problem: Do prior PEFT comparisons survive careful hyperparameter tuning?
core_method: Hyperparameter-tuned comparison of all major PEFT methods on VTAB-1K; cross-method error analysis
metrics: Top-1 accuracy; error type analysis; ensemble gain
key_evidence: ALL methods similar when tuned; complementary errors; PEFT preserves robustness better than full FT
limitations: VTAB-1K only; no multi-seed variance analysis
relevance_to_project: Template for diagnostic study methodology; also listed in Cluster A

title: AMLB: An AutoML Benchmark
research_problem: Rigorous reproducible evaluation of AutoML systems
core_method: 104 tasks; Docker containers; fixed time budgets; Friedman+Nemenyi statistical comparisons
key_evidence: AutoGluon SOTA; AutoGluon 5min > others 1h; only 4/24 LM benchmarks provide replication scripts
limitations: Docker overhead
relevance_to_project: Gold standard for rigorous AutoML evaluation

title: AutoML Benchmark with Shorter Time Constraints and Early Stopping
research_problem: Can time budgets as short as 5-30min preserve discriminative power?
core_method: Framework comparison across 5min→4h budgets; early stopping analysis
key_evidence: Rankings highly consistent (r>0.96 between 5min and 60min); early stopping saves 20-50% wall-time; 92% compute reduction
limitations: Limited to tested frameworks
relevance_to_project: Demonstrates that short budgets preserve HPO comparison validity; enables extensive reproducibility testing

title: UML Diagram Classification Dataset
research_problem: Curated duplicate-free UML diagram dataset for classification
core_method: 2626 images; 6 classes (activity/class/component/deployment/sequence/use case); Vision Transformers vs CNNs
key_evidence: ViT_h_14 92.7% accuracy; Component hardest (82.8% F1); Sequence easiest (97.7%)
limitations: Small dataset; UML only; single benchmark evaluation
relevance_to_project: Only public UML dataset but no SysML v2 equivalent exists

title: ArchCAD-400K: Open Large-Scale Architectural CAD Dataset
research_problem: Large-scale architectural CAD symbol spotting dataset
core_method: 413062 annotated chunks from 5538 drawings; 27 semantic categories; DPSS baseline
key_evidence: 70.6% PQ (10% over prior); 26x larger than FloorPlanCAD; only 14% residential
limitations: Architectural CAD only (not engineering)
relevance_to_project: Largest CAD dataset precedent; annotation pipeline methodology transferable

title: DrafterBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Civil Engineering Drawing Revision
research_problem: First benchmark for LLM agents on real-world technical drawing revision
core_method: 1920 tasks across 12 types from 20 real drawing projects; 46 PDF tools
key_evidence: Top model 79.9/100; ~20pt gap from simple to complex; overall task completion ~40%; single error→complete failure
limitations: PDF-specific; civil engineering domain only
relevance_to_project: Real-world engineering drawing benchmark with quantifiable failure modes

title: Enginuity: Engineering Diagram VLM Benchmark
research_problem: First open dataset for evaluating VLMs on complex engineering diagrams
core_method: 6940 pages; 18 vehicle subsystems; 6 diagram types; US military manuals
key_evidence: Recall@all 0.61-0.87 but Token F1pen only 0.03-0.18—systematic gap between identifying and describing parts
limitations: Military domain specificity; small QA set
relevance_to_project: Engineering VLM benchmark quantifying descriptive capability gap

title: Why Your Language Model is a Poor Implicit Reward Model? (Min-P Re-analysis)
research_problem: Can a high-profile ICLR Oral paper's claims survive proper statistical correction?
core_method: Re-analysis: included omitted data; Bonferroni correction; new independent human eval
code_available: After Bonferroni: 1/12 significant at 0.05/0/12 at 0.01; more participants preferred basic sampling
key_evidence: Re-analysis only; no new positive method
limitations: Blueprint for rigorous empirical science; documents common pitfalls in ML research

title: Pitfalls in Evaluating Inference-time Methods for Improving LLM Reliability
research_problem: Do inference-time methods consistently improve LLM reliability?
core_method: Systematic evaluation of CoT/Self-Consistency/ReAct/TreeOfThoughts/GraphOfThoughts/Multi-Agent Debate
key_evidence: **Each method had negative impact on at least one benchmark**; only 2 benchmarks showed avg improvement; no method consistently improved reliability
limitations: Method set limited; benchmarks may not represent all reliability dimensions
relevance_to_project: Template for negative-result diagnostic paper; structure is replicable for other subfields

title: Measuring What Matters: Construct Validity in LLM Benchmarks
research_problem: Do LLM benchmarks actually measure what they claim to measure?
core_method: Systematic review of 445 LLM benchmarks from 46114 articles; construct validity assessment
metrics: Construct validity presence/statistical test usage/sampling methodology
key_evidence: **Only 53.4% show any construct validity evidence; only 16% use statistical tests; 8 actionable recommendations**
limitations: Meta-review; no new benchmark
relevance_to_project: Checklist for designing any new benchmark; 8 recommendations should be mandatory

title: Train More Parameters But Mind Their Placement: PEFT Ablation
research_problem: Which LoRA adapter placement is optimal for language adaptation?
core_method: Systematic ablation of LoRA adapter placement (attention/feed-forward/layer-wise)
key_evidence: Feed-forward layers best; attention-layer LoRA underperforms; combining unnecessary; final 2 layers mitigate context degradation; more params consistently better
limitations: NLP only (language adaptation)
relevance_to_project: PEFT placement methodology template; shows that more params typically better

title: Empirical Evaluation of CO2 Emissions in BERT Fine-tuning
research_problem: Systematic quantification of carbon emissions in BERT fine-tuning
core_method: CO2 measurement via CodeCarbon; hyperparameter/GPU/batch size/model variant analysis
key_evidence: 15-40 kg CO2/run; 25% emission reduction via HP tuning; DistilBERT -45% CO2 for -2% accuracy; LoRA 7B: 57g CO2e for 21300 samples
limitations: Single model family (BERT); single benchmark framework
relevance_to_project: Quantifies energy-efficiency trade-off; LoRA emissions are negligible vs full FT

title: Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize ML Benchmarks
research_problem: Label errors are pervasive in benchmark test sets and distort model rankings
core_method: Confident Learning: estimates joint distribution of noisy and true labels via out-of-sample predicted probabilities
metrics: Label error rate/model accuracy change/ranking flips
key_evidence: 3.3% avg error across 10 benchmarks; ImageNet ~6% errors; 51% of CL-flagged candidates confirmed; ResNet-18 > ResNet-50 on corrected labels
limitations: Requires well-calibrated predicted probabilities; misses systematic errors
relevance_to_project: Foundational: CleanLab should be preprocessing step before any PEFT

title: Data-centric Artificial Intelligence: A Survey
research_problem: ML research over-emphasizes model innovation at expense of data quality
core_method: Taxonomy: training data development/inference data development/data maintenance across data lifecycle
key_evidence: First comprehensive data-centric AI survey; 242+ citations; identifies data quality as first-class concern
limitations: No empirical comparisons
relevance_to_project: Framework for why data quality matters as much as model architecture

title: DataPerf: Benchmarks for Data-Centric AI Development
authors: Mazumder et al. (45 authors incl. Andrew Ng)
research_problem: No standardized benchmarks for evaluating data-centric algorithms
core_method: Six tasks: training set creation/test set creation/selection/debugging/slicing/valuation
metrics: Task-specific (accuracy/F1 for selection; coverage/precision for slicing)
key_evidence: First community-led benchmark suite; sustained by MLCommons; enables reproducible data-cleaning comparison
limitations: Initial release 5 benchmarks; no LLM-specific data quality tasks; some need substantial compute
relevance_to_project: Evaluating data-cleaning as preprocessing before PEFT

title: BOXWRENCH: Benchmarking Weak Supervision on Realistic Tasks
research_problem: Existing WS benchmarks too simplistic; don't reflect real label noise
core_method: Realistic labeling functions with high class cardinality/domain expertise/multilingual LF reuse
key_evidence: Supervised learning needs 1000+ labeled examples to match weak supervision in realistic settings—critical for small-data budgets
limitations: Still synthetic approximation; may not capture all noise types
relevance_to_project: Weak supervision as alternative when clean labels are scarce

title: FHLR: Few-Shot Human-in-the-Loop Refinement for Label Noise
research_problem: Small sensor datasets suffer severe degradation under label noise; existing methods fail at high noise
core_method: Three-stage: seed training (label smoothing+EMA)→~100 expert-corrected labels→weighted parameter averaging
datasets: Sleep scoring/Activity recognition/Cardiac arrhythmia/Artifact detection (all small)
key_evidence: At 60% symmetric noise: FHLR 74.1% vs next best (LC) 30.2% (43-point gain); 19-31% improvement under asymmetric noise; robust to annotator disagreement
limitations: Requires ~100 expert labels; tested only on 1D sensor data
relevance_to_project: Directly models small-data+noise double challenge; budget-aware (only 100 expert labels needed)

title: BatMan-CLR: Making Few-Shot Meta-Learners Resilient Against Label Noise
research_problem: Meta-learners suffer catastrophic accuracy drops (up to 34%) under label noise during meta-training
core_method: Manifold+batch-manifold sampling transforms noisy supervised tasks into semi-supervised ones with contrastive loss
key_evidence: 60% wrong labels: accuracy drops limited to 1.1% (miniImageNet) and 9.4% (CIFAR-FS) vs 34% drop for baseline meta-learners
limitations: Only gradient-based meta-learners; contrastive loss adds compute; no cross-domain noise
relevance_to_project: Directly addresses few-shot+noise; intelligent sample selection improves robustness

title: APPN: Attention-based Pseudo-label Propagation for Noisy Few-Shot Learning
research_problem: FSL benchmarks assume clean labels but real few-shot tasks have noisy support sets
core_method: Attention mechanism distinguishes clean/noisy samples; pseudo-label propagation using latent class information
metrics: Few-shot accuracy under varying noise rates
key_evidence: Outperforms prior noise-robust FSL methods across Type I ID/Type II ID/OOD noise; interpretable attention-based noise detection
limitations: Graph propagation adds inference overhead; relies on attention quality
relevance_to_project: Practical reality: small support sets are often noisy; attention mechanism could inspire PEFT noise-filtering

title: Why LoRA Resists Label Noise: A Theoretical Framework
research_problem: LoRA shows empirical noise robustness but no theoretical explanation existed
core_method: 3 theorems: (1) Memorization bound—rank-r LoRA cannot memorize all labels when n>O(r(d+k-r)); (2) Optimal rank decreases with noise r*=O((n/(d(1+η)))^(1/(2α+1))); (3) Temporal separation—clean patterns early noise late. RACT algorithm for noise detection via rank discrepancy
key_evidence: 91.1% F1 noise detection on AG News; 91.46% accuracy maintained; lower rank recommended when noise suspected
limitations: Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed); single-author; moderate-scale datasets; RACT requires 2 adapters
relevance_to_project: CRITICAL: theoretical justification for low-rank LoRA under noise; optimal rank scaling with noise rate

title: Delora: Dual Low-Rank Adaptation for Noisy Label Detection
research_problem: Traditional small-loss sample selection creates vicious cycle where poor selection corrupts training
core_method: Dual LoRA: clean LoRA memorizes clean data + noisy LoRA memorizes mislabeled data; noisy LoRA output = learnable sample-dependent threshold; Stage 2 relabels with GPT-4o
key_evidence: +3.26% to +10% accuracy gain over standard LoRA under 20-40% noise; only +13.6MB params and +3.2GB memory; 84.53% at 60% symmetric noise
limitations: Relabeling stage requires GPT-4o API; tested primarily on text; dual LoRA adds modest training compute
relevance_to_project: CRITICAL: decoupling noise detection from classification in PEFT; directly implementable on RTX 5080 16GB

title: RFedLR: Robust Federated Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
research_problem: LoRA in FL suffers aggregation discrepancy and amplified label noise
core_method: Sensitivity-Aware Robust Tuning (only updates noise-sensitive params)+Adaptive Federated LoRA Aggregation (Fisher+noise sensitivity scoring)
metrics: Accuracy under SymFlip and PairFlip noise
key_evidence: 83.12% vs 75.28% (FedAvg+LoRA) at 20% PairFlip; 67.08% vs 56.93% (RoLoRA) at 40% PairFlip; only 0.1754% params updated; communication halved
limitations: Requires clean proxy dataset on server; FL-specific
relevance_to_project: Sensitivity-aware parameter selection concept adaptable to single-GPU RTX 5080

title: LoPE: Asymmetric LoRA with Poisoning MoE for Noise Robustness
research_problem: PEFT methods susceptible to noisy data; data cleaning is expensive
core_method: Asymmetric LoRA+dedicated poisoning expert in MoE; Stage 1: noise injection on poisoning expert; Stage 2: mask poisoning expert at inference
key_evidence: Achieves noise robustness WITHOUT any data cleaning pipeline; poisoning expert=noise absorber protecting main model
limitations: MoE adds parameters; requires generated noisy data for poisoning training; vision-focused
relevance_to_project: Novel paradigm: noise robustness via architectural design rather than preprocessing

title: Time-Consistency Curriculum for Instance-Dependent Noisy Labels
research_problem: Instance-dependent label noise causes most LNL methods to fail; simplistic difficulty measures
core_method: Joint noise-generating model+robust classifier; time-consistency curriculum: easy (temporally stable) → hard samples
key_evidence: SOTA on instance-dependent noise where most methods fail; time-consistency more reliable than loss-based heuristics
limitations: Two-model training doubles compute; requires prediction history; theoretical guarantees limited
relevance_to_project: Addresses hardest noise type; curriculum learning=inherently budget-aware

title: Survey on Data Quality Dimensions and Tools for ML
research_problem: Practitioners lack systematic understanding of DQ dimensions and tools
core_method: Reviews 17 DQ tools; 4 DQ dimensions (intrinsic/contextual/representational/accessibility) with 12 metrics
key_evidence: Identifies 17 DQ tools; highlights LLMs as emerging DQ evaluation approach; practical roadmap
limitations: Survey focus on tool landscape; no empirical comparison; rapidly evolving
relevance_to_project: 12-metric framework guides automated data quality scoring

title: Noise-Tolerant Deep Active Learning with Noisy Oracles
research_problem: Active learning assumes perfect oracles; real annotators/LLM oracles provide noisy labels
core_method: Consistency regularizer+angular margin loss+submodular batch diversity; multi-task framework
key_evidence: SOTA on classification+segmentation under noisy oracles; specifically addresses cold-start with small noisy labeled set
limitations: Submodular optimization complexity; angular margin requires tuning; assumes label-level noise
relevance_to_project: Budget-aware data acquisition: which samples to label when oracle is noisy?

title: Manifold DivideMix: Contrastive Learning for Severe Label Noise
research_problem: Standard DivideMix degrades under severe noise and can't handle OOD noisy samples
core_method: Self-supervised contrastive pretraining+KNN OOD removal+MixEMatch (mixup at input+manifold levels)
key_evidence: Maintains high accuracy at severe (>80%) noise where standard DivideMix collapses; MixEMatch stronger than MixMatch
limitations: Contrastive pretraining adds training time; KNN OOD may discard useful hard examples; workshop paper
relevance_to_project: Extends DivideMix for severe noise; contrastive pretraining adaptable for PEFT with noisy data

title: Survey on Learning from Data with Label Noise via Deep Neural Networks
research_problem: Fragmented LNL literature lacks unified taxonomy
core_method: Taxonomy: noise types (instance-independent symmetric/asymmetric/instance-dependent/human-annotated); methods (supervised/robust regression/loss adjustment/regularization/sample selection); benchmarks (CIFAR-10N/Clothing1M/WebVision)
key_evidence: Classifies LNL into 5 categories; extends beyond CV to fault diagnosis; semi-supervised+multimodal as emerging directions
limitations: Rapidly evolving; limited NLP LNL coverage
relevance_to_project: Entry point for LNL landscape; noise taxonomy helps diagnose which method to apply
